review_notes: I read the whole target file and compared its Layer section with the imported CatA/I112a.lean. I also checked the public variants (i112v_barLayer, i112v_layer_G, i112c_*) and i112f_comap_normalizer_barX. The three private lemmas diag_bar, diag_barLayer and diag_layer_G are proof-for-proof copies of cat_bar, cat_barLayer and cat_layer_G in I112a.lean, with the same statements, hypotheses and tactic scripts. The only difference I found is that cat_layer_G has an extra `eQ` binding, which diag_layer_G also has. The i112v_* and i112c_* variants have different hypotheses (GLStanding, IsSimpleGroup G), so they are not drop-in replacements. I also saw a smaller repeat, the pullback of non-normalization along the quotient map by i112f_comap_normalizer_barX. It occurs twice here and in about 15 other files. It is only about 5 lines, so I did not report it separately. The A and twistedA branches of i112d_diag2 are parallel, but they use different lemmas, so I did not report them. I could not compile anything, so the proposed change is untested. The main uncertainty is whether anything outside the two files depends on the names cat_* or diag_*.

findings.problem: The Layer section re-proves, line for line, three lemmas that the imported CFSG/LocalAnalysis/GLTheoremA/CatA/I112a.lean already proves. diag_bar is cat_bar (I112a lines 252–281). It passes to the quotient X/O_{p'}(X) and shows the K-group, p-rank, component and non-normalizing facts. This includes the argument that pulls non-normalization back through i112f_comap_normalizer_barX. diag_barLayer is cat_barLayer (I112a lines 284–332), which applies i112v_core, transports y into the quotient, derives hZL and hZ, and calls i112v_layer. diag_layer_G is cat_layer_G (I112a lines 334–371), which proves bClosure ≤ X, shows zpowers y is a 3-group, applies barX_inf_centralizer, lifts the layer and combines the equivalences. The statements, hypotheses and tactic scripts match. The only difference is the local name, because the I112a versions are `private` and so cannot be reused. The target imports I112a (line 3) and already uses i112StarAt_holds from it. That leaves about 120 lines of nontrivial group-theoretic proof in two places. A fix to one copy, for example if i112v_core or i112v_layer changes its signature, must be made in both.
findings.proposed_change: In I112a.lean, drop `private` from cat_bar, cat_barLayer and cat_layer_G. Rename them if you like, for example i112cat_bar, i112cat_barLayer and i112cat_layer_G. Both files are in namespace CFSG.LocalAnalysis.GLTheoremA and use the same `variable {G : Type} [Group G] [Finite G]`, so the statements are unchanged. In I112DiagMain.lean, delete diag_bar, diag_barLayer and diag_layer_G (lines 25–144), keeping `section Layer`/`end Layer` only if something is left in it. In i112DiagAt_holds, replace `diag_layer_G tables112_holds tableL2_unconditional tables112Types_holds tables112More_holds hX hB hBX hr hM hnM hbB hbn` by the same call to the shared lemma. The hypotheses in both places are `hX hB hBX hr hL hnL hyB hyn` and the conclusion has the same three components. The `obtain ⟨hcomp, -, hsimp⟩` pattern is unchanged. I also expect the `section Layer` `open` list and the imports of I112DiagChev/I112DiagL2 to need no change. I have not compiled this.
findings.benefit: This removes about 120 duplicated lines of proof that carry real mathematical content (quotient by the p′-core, the centralizer and layer lift, and the simple-group equivalence). It leaves one place to maintain, and the target file becomes a short statement of the diagonal-case classification. A reader no longer has to check that two long private proofs are really the same.
